title: FBI Crime Data Explorer (UCR, NIBRS, hate crime, arrests, police employees)
agency: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Criminal Justice Information Services Division (U.S. Department of Justice)
questions: violent crime rate trend in the United States
murders in a state by year
number of police officers per 1,000 people

key_only: more than 30 requests an hour or 50 a day (DEMO_KEY limits per IP address; a personal key allows 1,000 an hour)

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (each carries api.data.gov's public DEMO_KEY; replace it with your own free key if it answers OVER_RATE_LIMIT), save the JSON under the name shown, and upload the files. Without the links: the Crime Data Explorer at https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/ (Explorer > choose crime, location and years > download CSV) or its Documents & Downloads page for full NIBRS and SRS files.

cache.why: Small chart queries; CDE refreshes monthly and revises past years, so data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: Uniform Crime Reporting data published by the FBI are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); attribute the FBI UCR Program and do not imply endorsement.

citation: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Crime Data Explorer, {dataset}, api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde, retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: Counts depend on which agencies reported; 2021 coverage fell to about 77% of the population during the NIBRS transition, so a report must state coverage or participation.

clarify: Counts or rates? Counts depend on how many agencies reported (2021 coverage fell to about 77% of the population); compare years with rates per 100,000 and state the coverage.
Which years? 2021 is not comparable with earlier and later years at the state and national level because of the NIBRS transition; say whether to include or flag it.
Reported offenses (agency submissions, this pack) or the FBI's published national estimates (Crime in the Nation tables; not fetched by this pack)?
